description:
A STAGGER COSTS YOU SOMETHING. ONE RE-AIMED LOAD. This pack does NOT create a single extra fall - it makes the staggers that already happen actually interrupt the player, so contact has a consequence instead of being cosmetic. Test it AFTER falls-slide-tackle-contact.json, not at the same time.

WHAT CHANGES. match::anime::action::Stagger::vf32 (0x143f007b0) computes how many extra frames a stagger is LOCKED before the player may cancel out of it. The formula is extra = clamp(6 - floor(x*x*6), 0, 5) where x = clamp((Balance - 40)/60, 0, 1) and Balance is attribute 0x2a (read literally as 'mov edx,0x2a' at 0x143f00abb). This pack re-aims the load at 0x143f00af8 from the 6.0 pool cell to the 8.0 pool cell, which lengthens the lock for mid-to-high Balance players. The cell at 0x145ab244c is SHARED BY ROUGHLY 647 SITES (it is also the kick-error sigma cell) and is NOT written - only the instruction's own disp32 changes, so nothing else in the game is affected.

MEASURED EFFECT (a-EMULATED, re-run this pass). Balance -> extra locked frames:
    Balance:   40  50  60  70  75  80  85  88  90  92  95  97  99
    stock 6.0:  5   5   5   5   4   4   3   3   2   2   1   1   1
    THIS 8.0:   5   5   5   5   5   5   4   3   3   2   2   1   1
    (10.0):     5   5   5   5   5   5   5   4   4   3   2   1   1
So the change is 1 extra frame in the 75-95 Balance band and nothing at all below 70, where players are already pinned at the 5-frame cap. At 60 fps one frame is about 17 ms. STRONGER VERSION: 10.0 instead of 8.0 - re-aim 0x143f00af8 to cell 0x145a8dd7c, patch bytes F30F100D7CD2B801. Start at 8.0.

WHAT YOU SEE. Fewer instant recoveries. A shoulder that knocks a midfielder sideways costs him the next touch instead of nothing. This is a small, honest effect - do not expect drama from it.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE - your stick-controlled player, your AI team-mates and the CPU. Stagger::vf32 sits on exactly one vtable slot and every player runs it.

HOW IT WAS DEMONSTRATED. The arithmetic slice 0x143f00abb..0x143f00b73 was emulated under Unicorn on the INSTALLED image with ATTR_get (0x143ea8cb0) stubbed to return the Balance under test and the entry state reproduced from the real function (r14d=5 from 0x143f00874, ebx=0 from 0x143f00885, esi=1 from 0x143f00aa0, xmm6=0 from 0x143f00969, xmm7=60.0 from 0x143f00a3a, xmm8=1.0 from 0x143f0080a). Both re-aims were run as instruction overlays and produced the tables above. Independently this pass: the site bytes, the disp32 arithmetic and the value of every pool cell involved were recomputed from the raw image by hand.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. Balance does NOT decide whether you fall - it only ends a stagger that has already been chosen. Nothing in Stagger::vf32, Contact::vf2, Sliding::vf14 or either motion selector contains an RNG call or a Stagger-versus-FallDown test. If you are hoping this raises the odds of going to ground, it does not.

ALSO NOTE: the second Balance term in the same function (0x143f00b29-0x143f00b70) is INERT on this game's 40-99 attribute scale - it is gated on Balance > 99. Do not spend a second re-aim on it.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: NONE. Stagger::vf32 is never read by match::ai::Judge; the foul score is computed from the collision geometry, not from the reaction that follows it. No score term and no threshold is touched.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH. After a shoulder-to-shoulder or a clip, watch whether the player who got knocked can immediately play the ball again. Stock he usually can; with this he should lose a beat. Most visible on technical players in the 80-92 Balance band.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO STRONG. Your controlled player feeling unresponsive or 'stuck' after minor contact - at 8.0 you are giving up about 17 ms in that band, at 10.0 up to about 33 ms. If input feels laggy after bumps, revert. Also if midfielders start getting stacked up in repeated staggers and cannot clear the ball.

COLLISIONS: none. 0x143f00af8 is byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE (both F30F100D4C19BB01, verified this pass). Not in the applied kick-error bytes and not overlapping any unapplied spec.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/falls-stagger-lock-balance.json

patches.name: stagger lock-out curve 6.0 -> 8.0 (disp32 re-aim, shared cell NOT written)
patches.note: movss xmm1,[rip+0x1bb194c -> 0x145ab244c = 6.0] re-aimed to [rip+0x1c524bc -> 0x145b52fbc = 8.0]. disp32 recomputed by hand as 0x145b52fbc - 0x143f00b00 = 0x1c524bc. The 6.0 cell has ~647 referrers and is left untouched; only this instruction's displacement changes. Both cells confirmed to hold 6.0 and 8.0 in the installed image.
